subject: anatomy
title: Epithelium, cell junctions and glands

steps.tx: Epithelium is a sheet of cells that covers surfaces and lines cavities, ducts and glands. Classify it by layers and cell shape. **Simple** epithelium has one layer, **stratified** has several, and **pseudostratified** is one layer that looks layered because nuclei sit at different heights. Simple squamous lines alveoli, endothelium and mesothelium. Simple cuboidal lines thyroid follicles and ducts of glands. Simple columnar lines the stomach and large intestine.
steps.say: Epithelium is a sheet of cells that covers surfaces and lines cavities, ducts and glands. Classify it by layers and cell shape. Simple epithelium has one layer, stratified has several, and pseudostratified is one layer that looks layered because nuclei sit at different heights. Simple squamous lines alveoli, endothelium and mesothelium. Simple cuboidal lines thyroid follicles and ducts of glands. Simple columnar lines the stomach and large intestine.

steps.tx: Stratified and special epithelia are high yield. **Non-keratinised** stratified squamous lines the oral cavity, oesophagus, vagina and cornea. **Keratinised** stratified squamous forms the epidermis of skin. **Transitional** epithelium, also called urothelium, lines the renal pelvis, calyces, ureter and bladder. The membranous and penile urethra are lined by columnar epithelium, not urothelium.

steps.tx: Cell junctions hold cells together. **Tight junctions** seal neighbouring cells and stop molecules passing between them. **Desmosomes** are macula adherens and link intermediate filaments for mechanical strength. **Hemidesmosomes** anchor basal cells to the basement membrane through integrins. **Gap junctions** allow ions and small molecules to pass between cytoplasm, so cells can communicate.

steps.tx: Matching each site to its **epithelium** is a high-yield skill. The **ectocervix** is covered by non-keratinised **stratified squamous** epithelium, whereas the **endocervix** is lined by **simple columnar** cells that secrete mucus. The **cornea** and **conjunctiva** share the non-keratinised stratified squamous pattern, and the **olfactory mucosa** is **pseudostratified columnar**. The table summarises these pairings.
steps.say: Matching each site to its epithelium is a useful skill for exams. The ectocervix is lined by non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium, while the endocervix has simple columnar cells that secrete mucus. The cornea and conjunctiva both use non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium, and the olfactory mucosa is pseudostratified columnar. Learn these pairings as a set, and check the table for a quick recap.

steps.tx: Compare the **epithelium icons** side by side. One layer on the basement membrane is **simple**, several layers are **stratified**, and dome cells mark **transitional** epithelium. Cilia sit only on cells that reach the surface in pseudostratified epithelium. Match each icon to the site named under it.
